title: Baby Dodds - Wikipedia
notes: Warren 'Baby' Dodds, 24 Dec 1898 New Orleans - 14 Feb 1959. 'Regarded as one of the best jazz drummers of the pre-big band era'; kept the beat on the bass drum with buzz rolls on the snare; 'among the first drummers to be recorded improvising'. Influences Louis Cottrell Sr., Dave Perkins, Tubby Hall. Fate Marable riverboat band 1918-21 with Armstrong; King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band 1921-24; Armstrong's Hot Five and Hot Seven 1927; New Orleans revival in the 1940s.

title: Chick Webb - Wikipedia
notes: William Henry 'Chick' Webb, 10 Feb 1905 (disputed) Baltimore - 16 Jun 1939 Baltimore. Led his band in Harlem from 1926; Savoy Ballroom house band from 1931; battles of the bands with Goodman and Basie. Buddy Rich called him 'the daddy of them all'. Custom pedals, goose-neck cymbal holders, 28-inch bass drum. Featured Ella Fitzgerald from 1935; 'A-Tisket, A-Tasket'. Krupa credited him with paving the way for drummer-led bands; his solos 'paved the way for Buddy Rich and Louie Bellson'. Tommy Benford gave him lessons in New York.

title: Cozy Cole - Wikipedia
notes: William Randolph 'Cozy' Cole, 17 Oct 1909 East Orange NJ - 29 Jan 1981 Columbus, Ohio. Early drum solo on Jelly Roll Morton's 'Load of Cole' (1930). Cab Calloway 1938-42; CBS's first integrated radio orchestra 1942; Louis Armstrong All Stars. 'Topsy II' (1958) No. 3 Billboard Hot 100, No. 1 R&B, a long drum solo, one of the few drum solos to chart. Teacher of Philly Joe Jones; Cozy Powell took his nickname from him.

title: Dave Tough - Wikipedia
notes: David Jarvis Tough, 26 Apr 1907 Oak Park IL - 9 Dec 1948 Newark NJ. Austin High School Gang circle; 'the most important of the drummers of the Chicago circle'. Tommy Dorsey, Bunny Berigan, Benny Goodman (late 1930s); Artie Shaw's naval band 1942-44; Woody Herman's big band 1945. Big Band and Jazz Hall of Fame 2000.

title: George Wettling - Wikipedia
notes: George Godfrey Wettling, 28 Nov 1907 Topeka KS - 6 Jun 1968 New York. Heard King Oliver's band at Lincoln Gardens; Baby Dodds 'made a particular and lasting impression'. Big bands of Artie Shaw, Bunny Berigan, Red Norvo, Paul Whiteman; at his best with Eddie Condon and Muggsy Spanier; 'demonstrated the arts of dynamics and responding to a particular soloist that he had learned from Baby Dodds'. In 'A Jam Session at Victor' (1937). Later a painter influenced by Stuart Davis.

title: Jo Jones - Wikipedia
notes: Jonathan David Samuel Jones, 7 Oct 1911 Chicago - 3 Sep 1985. Count Basie Orchestra 1934-1948; the 'All-American Rhythm section' with Basie, Freddie Green, Walter Page. 'One of the first drummers to promote the use of brushes on drums, and shifting the role of timekeeping from the bass drum to the hi-hat cymbal.' Often omitted bass drum; continued ride rhythm on an opening and closing hi-hat; influenced the ride cymbal as timekeeper. Influence on Buddy Rich, Kenny Clarke, Roy Haynes, Max Roach, Louie Bellson. NEA Jazz Master 1985; Rifftide autobiography 2011.

title: Ray Bauduc - Wikipedia
notes: Ray Bauduc, 18 Jun 1906 New Orleans - 8 Jan 1988. Bob Crosby Orchestra and the Bobcats 1935-1942; co-wrote 'South Rampart Street Parade' (1937) and 'Big Noise from Winnetka' (1938) with Bob Haggart. Kept New Orleans two-beat drumming in a swing big band; woodblocks, cowbells, China cymbals, tom-toms; influenced by Baby Dodds. 'Helped New Orleans drummers make the transition into swing.'

title: Ray McKinley - Wikipedia
notes: Ray McKinley, 18 Jun 1910 Fort Worth TX - 7 May 1995. Dorsey Brothers 1934; Jimmy Dorsey to 1939; co-leader with Will Bradley 1939-42; 'Beat Me Daddy, Eight to the Bar' 1940 (sang); 'Eight Beat Mack' in 'Down the Road a Piece' (1940). Drummer then co-leader of the Major Glenn Miller Army Air Forces Orchestra after December 1944; led the new Glenn Miller Orchestra from 1956.

title: Sid Catlett - Wikipedia
notes: Sidney 'Big Sid' Catlett, 17 Jan 1910 Evansville IN - 25 Mar 1951 Chicago. 'One of the most versatile drummers of his era, adapting... as bebop emerged.' Studied the styles of Zutty Singleton, Baby Dodds and Jimmy Bertrand in Chicago. Fletcher Henderson, Don Redman, Benny Carter in the 1930s; Louis Armstrong's big band 1938-42; Armstrong's All-Stars 1947-49; on Dizzy Gillespie's 1945 recordings and the June 1945 Town Hall concert with Parker. Jammin' the Blues 1944 (dubbed by Jo Jones).

title: Sonny Greer - Wikipedia
notes: William Alexander 'Sonny' Greer, 13 Dec 1902 Long Branch NJ - 23 Mar 1982. Ellington's first drummer, the Washingtonians, the Cotton Club; with the orchestra until 1951. Designer for Leedy; huge kit with chimes, gong, timpani, vibes. Mercer Ellington: one of the few from whom Ellington took advice; 'great ear and unusual reflexes'.

title: Sonny Payne - Wikipedia
notes: Sonny Payne, 4 May 1926 - 29 Jan 1979. Son of drummer Chris Columbus; studied with Vic Berton. Erskine Hawkins 1950-53; Count Basie Dec 1954-Dec 1964 and later stints; Sinatra's drummer with Basie 1964-66; Harry James from 1966. Basie: 'Sonny Payne came in there, and right away he touched off a new spark in that band... you can hear and feel a difference in the band.' Harold Jones: took everything from him.

title: Tubby Hall - Wikipedia
notes: Alfred 'Tubby' Hall, 12 Oct 1895 Sellers LA - 13 May 1945 Chicago. New Orleans marching bands; Chicago from 1917; Carroll Dickerson, King Oliver, Jimmie Noone, Johnny Dodds; Armstrong's films A Rhapsody in Black and Blue and I'll Be Glad When You're Dead You Rascal You (1932). Krupa: Hall and Zutty Singleton 'knew every trick and just how to phrase the parts of the choruses behind the horns'. Hugues Panassié: one of the three greatest jazz drummers of his generation, with Singleton and Dodds. Brother Minor 'Ram' Hall.

title: Zutty Singleton - Wikipedia
notes: Arthur James 'Zutty' Singleton, 14 May 1898 Bunkie LA - 14 Jul 1975 New York. Papa Celestin, Fate Marable; Chicago with Jimmie Noone and Louis Armstrong's band with Earl Hines; 'landmark recordings with Louis Armstrong and his Hot Five' 1928-29; New York with Fats Waller, Jelly Roll Morton, Bechet; Los Angeles from 1943 (films, Orson Welles Almanac).

title: Louie Bellson - Wikipedia
notes: Louie Bellson, 6 Jul 1924 Rock Falls IL - 14 Feb 2009. 'Credited with pioneering the use of two bass drums' (from age 15). Won the Slingerland Gene Krupa contest at 17. Benny Goodman, Tommy Dorsey, Harry James, Duke Ellington in the 1940s-50s; married Pearl Bailey 1952; Jazz at the Philharmonic. Remo vice president. Modern Drummer Hall of Fame 1985. Cites Jo Jones, Sid Catlett, Chick Webb.

title: Ed Shaughnessy - Wikipedia
notes: Edwin Thomas Shaughnessy, 29 Jan 1929 Jersey City NJ - 24 May 2013 Calabasas CA. George Shearing, Charlie Ventura, Benny Goodman, Tommy Dorsey; Count Basie in the 1960s; The Tonight Show Band with Doc Severinsen. Drummer on Jimmy Smith's 'Bashin'' (1962) with 'Walk on the Wild Side'. Known for drum competitions with Buddy Rich; small groups with Mingus, Billie Holiday, Horace Silver; early Sesame Street orchestra.

title: Shadow Wilson - Wikipedia
notes: Rossiere 'Shadow' Wilson, 25 Sep 1919 - 11 Jul 1959. Swing orchestras: Lucky Millinder, Benny Carter, Lionel Hampton, Earl Hines, Count Basie, Woody Herman; later Illinois Jacquet, Erroll Garner, Thelonious Monk (1957 with John Coltrane), Ella Fitzgerald. Sat in at Minton's. Nickname from 'his beautiful light touch with brushes' (Peter Ind). Never recorded as leader.

title: Tony Sbarbaro - Wikipedia
notes: Antonio Sparbaro (Tony Sbarbaro / Tony Spargo), 27 Jun 1897 New Orleans - 30 Oct 1969 New York. Papa Jack Laine's Reliance Band; Original Dixieland Jazz Band from its first recordings in 1917 to the 1960s, leader from 1925. Woodblocks, cowbells, Chinese tom-toms; 'double-drumming', hitting the bass drum with the butt of the stick; kazoo on the kit. 'Darktown Strutters' Ball' (1917) in the Grammy Hall of Fame.

title: Louis Cottrell Sr. - Wikipedia
notes: Louis 'Old Man' Cottrell, 25 Dec 1878 - 17 Oct 1927, New Orleans. John Robichaux's orchestra 1909; Olympia Orchestra 1900-1915; Chicago with Manuel Perez 1916-18; A. J. Piron until his death. 'Credited as the innovator of the press roll in jazz drumming'; taught Alex Bigard, Baby Dodds, Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Freddie Kohlman, Cie Frazier and Alfred Williams.

title: Minor Hall - Wikipedia
notes: Minor 'Ram' Hall, 2 Mar 1897 Sellers LA - 16 Oct 1959 Sawtelle CA. Kid Ory in the mid-1910s; Superior Band; Chicago 1918; King Oliver 1921; Jimmie Noone 1926; Mutt Carey's Jeffersonians 1927-32; Kid Ory's Creole Jazz Band 1945-1956, 'one of his most longstanding members'; recorded extensively with Ory and with Armstrong in the 1940s. Brother of Tubby Hall.

title: Paul Barbarin - Wikipedia
notes: Adolphe Paul Barbarin, 5 May 1899 - 17 Feb 1969 New Orleans (died playing snare in a Mardi Gras parade). Chicago from 1917 with Freddie Keppard and Jimmie Noone; King Oliver 1925-27; Luis Russell's band from 1928, later backing Louis Armstrong; Red Allen 1942; Sidney Bechet 1944; founded the Onward Brass Band in 1955.

title: Bourbon Street Parade - Wikipedia
notes: Written by drummer Paul Barbarin in 1949; a Dixieland classic and New Orleans jazz standard, first performed by Paul Barbarin & His New Orleans Jazz Band; played at second line parades; Chris Barber's signature song from 1954.

title: Ben Pollack - Wikipedia
notes: Benjamin 'Ben' Pollack, 22 Jun 1903 Chicago - 7 Jun 1971 Palm Springs. New Orleans Rhythm Kings 1923 (co-wrote 'Tin Roof Blues'); Ben Pollack and his Californians from 1925; Park Central Orchestra in New York 1928; band broke up 1935 and became Bob Crosby's band. Employed Benny Goodman, Glenn Miller, Jack Teagarden, Jimmy McPartland, Harry James; nickname 'Father of Swing'.

title: Kaiser Marshall - Wikipedia
notes: Joseph 'Kaiser' Marshall, 11 Jun 1902 Savannah GA - 2 Jan 1948 New York. Raised in Boston, studied under George L. Stone. Fletcher Henderson's band 1922-1929. Later Ellington, Calloway, Bechet, Bunk Johnson, Mezzrow. Drummer on Louis Armstrong's 'Knockin' a Jug' (5 Mar 1929); McKinney's Cotton Pickers 1928-30.

title: Jimmy Crawford (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Jimmy 'Craw' Crawford, 14 Jan 1910 Memphis - 28 Jan 1980 New York. Jimmie Lunceford big band 1928-1942; later Broadway pits (Jamaica 1957-58). Modern Drummer: 'played with a strong, solid pulsation' and was 'a key factor in establishing the unique Lunceford beat.' Paul Motian named him a favourite.

title: O'Neil Spencer - Wikipedia
notes: William 'O'Neil' Spencer, 25 Nov 1909 - 24 Jul 1944. Mills Blue Rhythm Band 1931-36; John Kirby Sextet 1937-41 and 1942-43; died of tuberculosis. Credited (via a Jazz Profiles post and a Philly Joe Jones interview) with inventing the hi-hat in 1942, raising the low-hat. The article's claim is thinly sourced.

title: Cliff Leeman - Wikipedia
notes: Cliff Leeman, 10 Sep 1913 Portland ME - 26 Apr 1986. Nickname 'Mr. Time'. Artie Shaw 1938-39, Glenn Miller 1939, Tommy Dorsey 1939, Charlie Barnet 1940-43, Woody Herman 1943-44; John Kirby; Eddie Condon and Bobby Hackett in the 1950s; drumming on some of Bill Haley & His Comets' early recorded hits.

title: Panama Francis - Wikipedia
notes: David Albert 'Panama' Francis, 21 Dec 1918 Miami - 13 Nov 2001 Orlando. Roy Eldridge (who named him), Lucky Millinder from 1940, Cab Calloway 1947-52. In the 1950s a New York studio musician backing R&B and rock-and-roll: Bobby Darin 'Splish Splash', The Four Seasons, The Platters 'The Great Pretender', Dion 'Runaround Sue', Neil Sedaka, Jackie Wilson 'Reet Petite'. Revived the Savoy Sultans 1979.

title: J. C. Heard - Wikipedia
notes: James Charles Heard, 10 Aug 1917 Dayton OH - 27 Sep 1988 Royal Oak MI. Teddy Wilson 1939; Cab Calloway 1942-45 (Stormy Weather); Jazz at the Philharmonic; Japan from 1953, teaching; Detroit from 1966, mentor. 'Heard's style was a hybrid of swing and bop'; 'known for his innovative techniques and the hard swing he would bring to both large and small bands.' Mary Lou Williams Zodiac Suite 1945. J.C. Heard JazzWeek@Wayne.

title: Sam Woodyard - Wikipedia
notes: Sam Woodyard, 7 Jan 1925 Elizabeth NJ - 20 Sep 1988 Paris. Largely self-taught. Duke Ellington's orchestra 1955-1966: At Newport (1956), A Drum Is a Woman, Such Sweet Thunder (1957), Black, Brown and Beige (1958). Later Ella Fitzgerald, Buddy Rich, Claude Bolling.

title: Ellington at Newport - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 7 July 1956; released November 1956 on Columbia. Paul Gonsalves's solo in 'Diminuendo and Crescendo in Blue' 'backed only by bassist Jimmy Woode, drummer Sam Woodyard, and Ellington'; 'a concert which revitalized Ellington's flagging career'. Woodyard's drum feature 'Skin Deep'. National Recording Registry 2022.

title: Mel Lewis - Wikipedia
notes: Mel Lewis (Melvin Sokoloff), 10 May 1929 Buffalo - 2 Feb 1990 New York; fourteen Grammy nominations. Stan Kenton 1954; Los Angeles 1957; New York 1963; co-led the Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra from 1966 at the Village Vanguard on Monday nights; Mel Lewis and the Jazz Orchestra from 1978, now the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra. Cymbal work unique; Buddy Rich: 'Mel Lewis doesn't sound like anybody else.' Played to support, not force: 'If you watch me, it doesn't look like I'm doing much.' Live in Munich (1976) won a Grammy.

title: Don Lamond - Wikipedia
notes: Donald Douglas Lamond Jr., 18 Aug 1920 Oklahoma City - 23 Dec 2003 Orlando. Took over Dave Tough's place in Woody Herman's First Herd in 1945; Second Herd until 1949; Charlie Parker sessions 1947 (Dial) and 1952; then a session musician 'recording in a wide variety of styles' (549 sessions 1943-1982 per Lord). Book First Call Drummer: Don Lamond.

title: Viola Smith - Wikipedia
notes: Viola Clara Smith (née Schmitz), 29 Nov 1912 - 21 Oct 2020 (aged 107). 'One of the first professional female drummers.' Schmitz Sisters Family Orchestra; The Coquettes 1938-42; Phil Spitalny's Hour of Charm Orchestra 1942-54; Kit Kat Band in Broadway's Cabaret 1966-70; five Ed Sullivan Show appearances; Truman's 1949 inauguration. 1942 Down Beat article 'Give Girl Musicians a Break!'. Billed as the 'fastest girl drummer'. Films When Johnny Comes Marching Home (1942), Here Come the Co-Eds (1945).

title: Pauline Braddy - Wikipedia
notes: Pauline Braddy Williams, 14 Feb 1922 - 28 Jan 1996. Drummer of the International Sweethearts of Rhythm, an integrated, all-female swing band, 1939-1955; known as 'Queen of the Drums'.

title: International Sweethearts of Rhythm - Wikipedia
notes: Braddy a charter (1937) member, 'tutored on drums by Sid Catlett and Jo Jones'. Singles 'Jump Children'/'Slightly Frantic' (1945) and others; compilation Hottest Women's Band of the 1940s (Hot Licks 1944-1946) selected for the National Recording Registry in 2012; soundies 1946-47.

title: Jimmy Bertrand - Wikipedia
notes: Jimmy Bertrand, 24 Feb 1900 Biloxi MS - Aug 1960 Chicago. Chicago blues and jazz scene of the 1920s; recorded with Louis Armstrong, Johnny Dodds, Erskine Tate, Blind Blake; led Jimmy Bertrand's Washboard Wizards; 'a noted instructor', students Wallace Bishop, Lionel Hampton, Big Sid Catlett.

title: Chauncey Morehouse - Wikipedia
notes: Chauncey Morehouse, 11 Mar 1902 Niagara Falls NY - 31 Oct 1980 Medford NJ. Paul Specht 1922-24; Jean Goldkette 1925-27; Adrian Rollini 1927; Don Voorhees 1928-29; recorded 1927-29 with Frankie Trumbauer, Bix Beiderbecke, Red Nichols, the Dorsey Brothers, Joe Venuti. Around 1932 invented the N'Goma drums, '14 chromatically tuned snare drums mounted on a circular bar'; 1938 a chromatically tuned percussion ensemble with Stan King. Studio work from 1929.

title: Jack Parnell - Wikipedia
notes: John Russell Parnell, 6 Aug 1923 London - 8 Aug 2010 Southwold. Vic Lewis and the Lewis-Parnell Jazzmen 1944-46 ('Ugly Child'); 'voted best drummer in the Melody Maker poll for seven years in succession'; Jack Parnell Orchestra 1951-58; ATV musical director 1956-1981; Sunday Night at the London Palladium; conductor of The Muppet Show orchestra; Emmy 1974.

title: Tommy Benford - Wikipedia
notes: Tommy Benford, 19 Apr 1905 Charleston WV - 24 Mar 1994 Mount Vernon NY. Jenkins Orphanage band (toured England 1914); recorded with Jelly Roll Morton 1928 and 1930; Ellington, Fats Waller, Eddie South; Europe 1932-41, including the 1937 Paris session with Coleman Hawkins, Benny Carter, Django Reinhardt and Stephane Grappelli. Played for 60 years.

title: Dottie Dodgion - Wikipedia
notes: Dorothy Rosalie Giaimo, 23 Sep 1929 Brea CA - 17 Sep 2021 Pacific Grove CA. Carl Fontana in Las Vegas late 1950s; New York 1961: Benny Goodman, Tony Bennett, Marian McPartland, Zoot Sims, Al Cohn; Ruby Braff, Joe Venuti; McPartland's all-female group 1977; Monterey from 1984. Memoir The Lady Swings: Memoirs of a Jazz Drummer (University of Illinois Press, 2021). NYT obituary: 'A Standout Drummer in More Ways Than One'.

title: Ronnie Verrell - Wikipedia
notes: Ronnie Verrell, 21 Feb 1926 Rochester, Kent - 22 Feb 2002 Kingston-upon-Thames. Ted Heath Orchestra Sept 1951 to 1964 (US tour 1956; 'Hot Toddy', 'Hawaiian War Chant' solo); Jack Parnell's ATV house band; Syd Lawrence Orchestra 1980-c.2000. Drummed as 'Animal' on The Muppet Show. Daily Telegraph: 'Britain's best-known big band drummer for half a century'; The Scotsman: 'driving band drummer' and 'exciting soloist'.

title: Sherrie Maricle - Wikipedia
notes: Sharon Lee Maricle, born 2 Sep 1963 Buffalo NY. NYU PhD 2000; director of percussion studies at NYU late 1980s; Village Gate jam sessions 1987-93; leads the DIVA Jazz Orchestra, DIVA Jazz Trio and Five Play; I Believe In You (2000), Live in Concert (2002). Lifetime Achievement Award, Mary Lou Williams Women in Jazz Festival, 2009.

title: Specs Powell - Wikipedia
notes: Gordon 'Specs' Powell, 5 Jun 1922 New York - 15 Sep 2007 San Diego. Edgar Hayes 1939; Benny Carter 1941-42; 'the first black staff musician hired by CBS in 1943'; Ed Sullivan Show percussion early 1960s; commissioned possibly the first bongo stand from Martin Cohen (LP); Big Band Jazz Hall of Fame 2004. Sessions with Erroll Garner (The Most Happy Piano, 1957), Nina Simone, Carla Thomas, Moondog.
